turns: Last week at the museum a school group asked who built the old mill, and I ended up telling them about the strike of 1912 instead. I always find the door the textbook left shut.

The council voted on the bus route without asking the people who ride it. I wrote three pages and then took the notes to the library, not the meeting. I do not like being the loud one, but I do not like silence either.
My sister says I turn dinner into a seminar. Maybe. But I would rather be a little too much than leave a thing unsaid that someone needed to hear.
When someone asks me straight what I think, I give them a book title. It feels safer than a verdict.
Tuesday was a bad one. We got there late, and I sat in the truck afterward for twenty minutes with the engine off. Nobody saw. I made coffee and acted like it was fine.
I took the double shift that nobody wanted, again. If I am moving I do not have to think about the quiet. Then I get home and the quiet is waiting anyway.
My daughter drew me a card with a blanket on it. I keep it in the glovebox. I did not tell her why it got to me.
I told my supervisor I was fine. I am not sure what I wanted him to say. I think I wanted him to ask twice.
Fine. Work was fine. The night shift is quiet.
My brother has an exam Friday. I made his lunches for the week on Sunday. He does not know I check his schedule.
I keep the receipts for his school stuff in a folder. If anyone asks, I can show them. Nobody asks.
When he says thanks I say it is nothing. It is not nothing, but I do not say that.
Before I answer, why do you ask? I will tell you, I just like to know what a question is for. Okay, so: my week was mostly editing someone else's piece down to half its size.
I turned down a story last month because the source wanted to read my draft first. I would rather lose the story than hand over the pen.
My friend asked what I wanted for my birthday and I asked what she wanted to give. She laughed. I think I do this to stay level with people.
I like when a conversation goes both ways. If it is only me talking I start to feel like an exhibit.
The new housing rule came up at lunch and I went quiet. I have opinions, but I have watched friendships end over this exact thing, so I count the room first.
I volunteer at the food bank on Saturdays. Nobody there asks how I vote. That is part of why I keep going.
My uncle sends me articles every morning. I read them all and answer none. Replying feels like signing something.
I think people can disagree and still carry each other's groceries. I would like to live in that kind of town.
I still set the table for two on Sundays and then put one plate back. Forty years of habit. I have decided to let it be habit rather than sorrow.
I joined the garden club mostly for something to do on Thursdays. Now I know which neighbor's tomatoes come in first, and that feels like something.
My grandson asked what I did all day. I said I watered things and waited for the post. He found that very funny. I did too.
What matters to me now is being a person someone could knock on the door of without calling first.
So we pivoted again, which reminds me of when I tried to learn the cello. I quit after three weeks because I could not stand being bad at it in front of people.
I told the team the launch was on track. It was on track the way a train is on track when the bridge is out. I did not want to be the one to say it.
My cofounder is great at the deck and the pitch. I am great at the spreadsheet nobody opens. I keep the numbers to myself until they are good.
I would rather be the person who fixed it quietly than the one who raised the flag early. I know that is probably backwards.
My mother calls every evening at seven. I pick up even when I am in the middle of cooking. If I miss it I call back within the hour, always.
I moved back to be near my parents. My partner said it was my choice, and it was, but it did not feel like one when I made it.
At the family dinner my aunt asked when I would settle down. I smiled and passed the rice. I rehearsed an answer in the car on the way home.
I send money home on the first of the month. I have never told anyone how much. It is not a secret, it is just mine.
I came out to my dentist before my parents, which tells you everything about my priorities. It felt easy to say to someone who could not answer back.
At work I am the funny one. If a meeting gets tense I do a bit. Last Monday I did a bit and then realized nobody had finished their point.
My partner says I joke when I am scared. I said that is ridiculous, and then made a joke about it.
I want one room where I do not have to be entertaining. I think that might be the kitchen at two in the morning.
When we left we had two bags. I still keep a small bag packed in the hall closet. My wife knows. We do not talk about it.
I count what is in the account every Friday. It is not about being rich. It is about knowing that if we had to go again, we could go.
My boss offered me a promotion and I asked about the contract first. He laughed. I did not explain.
I tell my kids to learn things that fit in your head, because those travel. A degree is paper; what you can do with your hands stays.
Midterms are this week. I have a plan on a sticky note and a second plan on the back of it in case the first one falls apart.
My roommate asked me to go out and I said I had a paper. I did not have a paper. I just needed the evening to be mine.
I do not like when people comment on how I look, even when it is kind. I change the subject to the weather.
I do my best thinking walking, so I walk the long way to campus. Nobody has to know why it takes me forty minutes.
I want to be left alone and I want someone to notice I am gone. Both. Every weekend.
I say I hate surprises, and then I get annoyed when nobody plans anything for my birthday. I know how that sounds.
I told my brother I did not care about the promotion. I cared a lot. I stayed late three nights to make sure it looked like I did not.
People call me easygoing. I am only easygoing about things I have already decided not to want.
Sorry, my English is, how to say, slower in the feelings. In my country we cook together on Sunday. Here I cook for one and it is too much food.
I teach my daughter the old songs even if she answers in English. I think if she forgets the song, a small door closes.
At the school meeting I did not speak. I had the words ready, but by the time I was sure of the grammar the topic had moved.
My neighbor brought bread when we moved in. It was the first time I understood this place could be home. I want to be someone who also brings bread.
I run the Thursday supper at the church hall. Twenty people last week, four of them new. I counted the chairs twice because I do not want anyone standing.
When the oven broke I did not ask for help, I just made sandwiches. Someone said I should have called. I said the sandwiches were fine.
I do not like being thanked in front of everyone. I would rather someone quietly bring a pie next week.
I think a place is only a community if someone notices when you stop coming.
I get up at five to do his bottles and then I go to school. The teacher thinks I am zoning out. I am actually doing math in my head about the week.
My mom helps, but I do not like asking. I put a list on the fridge instead, so she can see what is needed without me saying it.
I do not tell people at school I have a kid. Not because I am ashamed. I just do not want to be the story.
When he laughs at the dumbest thing, nothing else matters. I try to remember that on the bad days.
A colleague padded his expense report and everyone knows. I keep my receipts to the cent, and I am angry that it feels foolish to.
I returned a wallet last month with the cash in it. My friend said I should have kept a twenty for the trouble. I did not argue, I just felt tired.
I would rather lose an argument honestly than win it with a trick. I have lost a few.
When I see someone cutting a corner I feel it in my chest before I decide what to do. Most of the time I decide to say nothing, and I carry it home.
